description: Implement a real 3-state (closed/open/half-open) circuit breaker in place of a stub that always calls through
prompts: breaker.py's CircuitBreaker.call(fn, now) always just calls fn() - there is no breaking logic at all. Implement the real 3-state machine: __init__(self, failure_threshold, reset_timeout). Starts CLOSED. In CLOSED, call(fn, now) invokes fn(); if it raises, count consecutive failures, and once `failure_threshold` CONSECUTIVE failures have happened, trip to OPEN (recording when it opened) and re-raise the exception that caused the trip. While OPEN, call(fn, now) must NOT invoke fn() at all and must instead raise CircuitOpenError - UNLESS at least `reset_timeout` seconds have passed since it opened, in which case it moves to HALF_OPEN and allows exactly ONE trial call: if that call succeeds, go back to CLOSED (reset the failure count); if it raises, go back to OPEN and RESET the open-time to `now` (so the next trial is only allowed after another full reset_timeout, not immediately).

import pytest

from breaker import CircuitBreaker, CircuitOpenError


def _boom():
    raise RuntimeError('boom')


def test_trips_open_after_consecutive_failures():
    b = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=3, reset_timeout=10)
    for _ in range(3):
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            b.call(_boom, now=0)
    with pytest.raises(CircuitOpenError):
        b.call(lambda: 'should not run', now=0)


def test_fails_fast_without_calling_fn_while_open():
    b = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=1, reset_timeout=100)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        b.call(_boom, now=0)
    calls = []
    with pytest.raises(CircuitOpenError):
        b.call(lambda: calls.append(1), now=1)
    assert calls == []


def test_half_open_trial_after_timeout_success_closes():
    b = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=1, reset_timeout=10)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        b.call(_boom, now=0)
    assert b.call(lambda: 'ok', now=10) == 'ok'
    # closed again: a fresh single failure must not trip it (threshold=1 but count reset)
    assert b.call(lambda: 'still-fine', now=11) == 'still-fine'


def test_half_open_failure_reopens_and_resets_clock():
    b = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=1, reset_timeout=10)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        b.call(_boom, now=0)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        b.call(_boom, now=10)  # half-open trial fails -> reopens, clock resets to 10
    with pytest.raises(CircuitOpenError):
        b.call(lambda: 'too soon', now=15)  # only 5s since the reopen at t=10
    assert b.call(lambda: 'ok now', now=20) == 'ok now'
